how: London Archers run beginner courses in winter and have-a-go sessions in summer, shooting indoors in Pimlico and outdoors near Kensington Palace; other clubs include 2020 Archery at London Bridge.
Kimber Skatepark in Wandsworth combines a skatepark and BMX track, and BMX riders also use Southbank.
Dedicated bouldering gyms include HarroWall, VauxWall, The Arch (Bermondsey, Acton, Edgware) and The Climbing Hangar, with shoe rental.
Adult cricket clubs and leagues operate across London, including Regent's Park Cricket Club and Last Man Stands adult leagues.
Queens Ice and Bowl in Queensway has curling lanes on its ice rink.
Welsh Harp Sailing Club, Wembley Sailing Club and Sea Cadets sail dinghies on the Brent Reservoir in north-west London.
Central London Fencing Club teaches beginners at Greycoat Hospital School; most London clubs offer a taster session before a multi-week beginner course.
London GAA runs Gaelic football and hurling clubs (e.g. Dulwich Harps, Brothers Pearse) with county grounds at McGovern Park in Ruislip.
Hyde Park Stables offers arena riding lessons and courses for all abilities with no prior experience needed.
Lee Valley Ice Centre offers ice hockey and Alexandra Palace hosts regular ice hockey matches.
Year-round rinks include Alexandra Palace, Lee Valley Ice Centre, Streatham Ice Arena and Queens in Queensway, plus seasonal rinks at Somerset House.
Roped climbing with an induction is available at Westway Climbing Centre, The Castle Climbing Centre and Mile End Climbing Wall.
The Budokwai in Knightsbridge is a long-established judo club with beginner programmes; Sobell and Ealing judo clubs also operate.
Central London Lacrosse runs junior and adult teams based at the Regent's Park and Primrose Hill hub.
Go Mammoth, Netbusters and Power Play run beginner and social netball leagues at many London venues.
Dozens of padel clubs operate across London including Padium (Canary Wharf), Stratford Padel Club and pay-and-play public courts in Regent's Park and Hyde Park.
The Padel Yard in Wandsworth lists an outdoor pickleball court; pickleball provision in London is still limited.
Adult rugby union clubs such as Belsize Park RFC play in Regent's Park; many more clubs exist across the metro area.
Southbank Undercroft is a famous skate spot, with further skateparks at Kimber (Wandsworth), Bay 66 and Cantelowes.
Taekwondo classes for beginners run at Elite Taekwon-Do (Kensington, Wembley), the Traditional Taekwondo Association (Peckham, Southwark) and London Taekwondo Warriors.
UK Ultimate lists clubs and runs tournaments at London venues such as Redbridge and Cranford; its find-a-club page covers London teams.
London has many council and private allotments, with demand at a record high according to a London Assembly report, including long-running sites such as Manor Garden Allotments in Hackney Wick.
Wild Food UK runs foraging courses in the Surrey fringe of London including an autumn course at Warlingham.

how: Geocaching.com lists caches across London; its map defaults to central London.
The Capital Ring is a roughly 125 km waymarked circular walking route through London parks and green spaces, joinable at any point.
The tidal Thames foreshore can be explored at low tide, but searching it requires a Port of London Authority permit.
Epping Forest permits mountain biking on its single-track trails, with clubs riding on Sunday mornings.
Orienteering is a popular activity in Epping Forest on the north-east edge of London.
The London Wetland Centre in Barnes is a major birdwatching site where sparrowhawks are among the species seen; large raptors are rare in the city.

Hampstead Observatory is open to the public on winter Friday and Saturday evenings and Sunday mornings with volunteers from the Hampstead Scientific Society; the Royal Observatory Greenwich also has telescopes and a planetarium.
Wild Food UK runs autumn foraging courses near London at Warlingham and in Surrey and Kent woodland.

how: Fishing is permitted in some of the Highgate Ponds on Hampstead Heath; Lee Valley and Thames venues also exist.
Greater London is flat with no suitable ridge launch sites; the nearest hang gliding is on the South Downs or Chilterns escarpments, roughly 1 to 1.5 hours away.
Lee Valley White Water Centre at Waltham Cross offers canoeing and kayaking on Olympic and intermediate courses for all abilities.
Parliament Hill on Hampstead Heath is known as Kite Hill because it suits kite flying.
Rowing boats and pedalos, including electric and accessible pedalos, can be hired on the Serpentine in Hyde Park.
Thames Rowing Club has rowed from Putney Embankment since 1860; many other tidal Thames clubs exist.
Welsh Harp Sailing Club and Wembley Sailing Club run sailing on the Brent Reservoir, and Phoenix Canoe Club offers sailing and canoeing there.
Greater London is inland with no ocean waves; the nearest regular surf is on the south coast around Bournemouth, roughly 2 to 2.5 hours away.
RADA offers adult short courses in acting, improvisation and Meisner technique, some with no audition required.
The Royal Academy of Dance in London lists termly adult ballet classes; many other studios offer adult beginner ballet.
The Bhavan Centre stages Bharatanatyam performances and teaches Indian classical dance; a regular class timetable is on its site.
Pineapple Dance Studios in Covent Garden offers around 400 weekly open classes in over 40 styles, which include street dance.
Morley College London offers Vocal Studies and Choirs courses open to adults.
Point Blank Music School in London teaches DJing and music production courses.
Hoopla Impro runs beginner-friendly improv classes (Levels 1-5) and drop-in workshops in central London; The Comedy Store Players perform weekly.
Bhavan Centre in West Kensington hosts Kathak workshops and productions alongside Indian dance and music classes.
Lion dances are performed in Chinatown around Chinese New Year; no regular classes were confirmed.
The Magic Circle's headquarters hosts regular close-up magic shows and tours, but its classes are for ages 10-18 only.
Point Blank Music School in London teaches music production and electronic music courses.
University of the Arts London short courses include an Animation, interactive, film and sound category taught in London.
London Centre for Book Arts in Hackney runs workshops and a making-books school with a bindery available to studio members.
Four Corners in Bethnal Green runs community darkroom facilities for film printing.
Loop Knitting in Islington runs Embroidery and Textile classes and hand-stitching workshops.
University of the Arts London short courses include an accessories and jewellery category in London.
Loop Knitting in Camden Passage runs knitting and crochet classes.
Morley College London offers Painting and Drawing courses for adults.
University of the Arts London short courses include a Photography category covering digital photography in London.
Turning Earth runs six- to twelve-week all-level hand-building and wheel courses at studios in Hoxton, Leyton and Highgate.
